evidence: Read original released MISATO checkpoint on CPU using its unmodified original source and existing NumPy1.26 overlay; no inference, training, reference edits or new environment install.

pvb.loss_observation: Original _train adds a separate ligand MSE on top of masked all-atom MSE, for both velocity and drift. Static and MD use the same encoder/decoder; target switches from clean input to next frame. Not numerically identical to Molvid's half-protein/half-ligand loss.

conclusions: Current Molvid is not smaller than released MISATO PVB by total parameter count. This does not establish adequate effective capacity.

Capacity allocation and geometric computation differ materially: PVB repeats current-coordinate equivariant edge messages8 times in its decoder; Molvid's expensive DiT includes time/history and pooled-block attention, plus two observed-geometry local message blocks.
Do not compare the query encoder parameter count alone against the entire PVB: Molvid DiT and readout also process geometric information.
Existing4-to8 DiT expansion held geometry message block count fixed, so its negative result does not refute a deeper atom-geometric backbone.

The concrete gain from complex data/role balancing and the untested main-static curriculum take priority over another unconditioned increase in total parameters. Geometric depth is a distinct subsequent capacity hypothesis, not a proven fix.
status: architecture evidence only; no new efficacy claim or default merge
